verdicts.quote: “To use an API key, pass an Authorization header with a value of Bearer <Your-API-Key-Here>.”
verdicts.reason: Docs show Bearer API key auth as the standard for the v3 API; Basic auth is not supported for username/password. ([static1.twilio.com](https://static1.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/for-developers/sending-email/authentication))

verdicts.quote: “Twilio SendGrid's free trial runs $0 for 60 days and lets you send 100 emails a day — no credit card, no commitment.”
verdicts.reason: New accounts get self‑serve credentials on a 60‑day trial; free plans were retired in 2025, so continued sending requires upgrading. ([twilio.com](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/email-api/pricing))

verdicts.quote: “The SendGrid API endpoints allow you to… send transactional emails, create marketing campaigns, manage your contacts, and monitor the health of your email statistics.”
verdicts.reason: The API covers many resources (mail send, contacts, marketing, suppressions, templates, stats, subusers, IPs, webhooks), i.e., broad. ([twilio.com](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference))

verdicts.quote: “Built and maintained by a SendGrid engineer, as an independent project — not an official SendGrid product.”
verdicts.reason: Confirms an MCP server exists but is community‑built, not vendor‑official. ([github.com](https://github.com/deyikong/sendgrid-mcp))

verdicts.quote: “After the 60-day period, you'll need to upgrade your plans to continue sending emails or to access the Marketing tab in the dashboard.”
verdicts.reason: Self‑serve creds and full docs make it buildable now, but the 60‑day trial caps (e.g., 100 emails/day; 100 contacts) and post‑trial upgrade need mean ready_with_caveats; blocker: paid_plan. ([twilio.com](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/account-and-settings/upgrading-your-plan?save_locale=en))
